close_reason: Decision recorded in comment (Option 3, attended session 2026-05-12): ship two functions verify_tls_client_dns(Option<&ServerName>) + verify_tls_client_mailbox(Option<&MailboxName>). Implementation lives under parent PKIX-fmtv.11.2's client half.
description:
PKIX-fmtv.7's (D1) resolution constrains identity args to pre-parsed `&ServerName<'_>` / `&MailboxName<'_>`. It does not pin down which (or both) `verify_tls_client` accepts. The original bead description on .11.2 suggested an enum `ClientIdentity<'_>` but (D1) ruled out introducing new identity types in this round.

TLS client auth identity in practice:

- **EAP-TLS / device certs:** identity in subject DN, rarely SAN. Neither `ServerName` nor `MailboxName` fits.
- **Personal S/MIME client certs (very common):** identity is mailbox (rfc822Name SAN). `MailboxName` fits.
- **Service-to-service mTLS (common):** identity is DNS-name (dNSName SAN). `ServerName` fits.

Candidate shapes (all consistent with (D1)):

1. **`Option<&MailboxName<'_>>`** — covers personal S/MIME flow. Service-to-service mTLS must drop to `verify_chain` + `verify_dns_name` manually.
2. **`Option<&ServerName<'_>>`** — covers service mTLS. S/MIME flow must drop to `verify_chain` + `verify_mailbox` manually.
3. **Two separate fns:** `verify_tls_client_mailbox(..., mailbox: &MailboxName)` and `verify_tls_client_dns(..., name: &ServerName)`. Both ship; caller picks at call site by name. Cleanest type discipline, larger API surface.
4. **`Option<&dyn SomeIdentityTrait>`** — introduces a new abstraction. Violates 'no new identity types beyond ServerName / MailboxName' implied by (D1).

`verify_tls_server` (the matching pair) is now shipped at `pkix_chain::verify_tls_server` taking `&ServerName<'_>`. The asymmetry between server and client is unavoidable since TLS client auth identity types are inherently more varied than server identity (where DNS / IP literal cover essentially everything).

Recommendation (mine, low confidence): option 3 (two separate functions). It avoids `Option<>` (TLS client auth without identity binding is rare in practice — those callers can just call `verify_chain` directly), preserves type discipline, and lets the function name communicate the binding shape at the call site (`verify_tls_client_mailbox` is self-documenting). Cost: doubles the wrapper count from 7 to 8.

Asking Mark to pick. Once decided, ship the wrapper(s) and close this bead + the parent .11.2 client half.
title: verify_tls_client identity shape clarification
